market_summary: US August PCE came in soft: core +0.2% m/m and 3.0% y/y (consensus 3.3%), headline +0.3% m/m and 3.4% y/y, while personal spending jumped 0.9% and Q2 GDP was revised up to 2.2% annualised from 1.5%, with data-centre structures among the upward revisions. October Fed hike odds dropped to about 36% (hold 64%) from 51% a day earlier and 71% a week ago, helped by NY Fed's Williams saying there is 'no need for urgency'; the fed funds target is 3.75-4.00%. The 10-year yield dipped to 5.24% on the print but was back at 5.28% by 10:37 ET (prior close 5.26%), ending a September in which it rose 47bp, the biggest monthly move in about two years; the dollar index eased 0.15% to 100.96 after a near 2% September gain. At 10:30 ET the S&P 500 was 7,706 (+0.45%), Nasdaq 27,070 (+1.0%), but SOX lagged at 12,559 (-0.55%) despite Nvidia +1.5% and Intel +2.6%; Alphabet +2.2%, Constellation Energy -5.7%; VIX 15.9. Asia Wednesday: ASX 200 8,789 (+0.9%), Nikkei 66,754 (+1.9%), Kospi 6,838 (-0.5%), Hang Seng 24,613 (+0.4%), Shanghai 3,842 (+0.3%) in its last session before the Oct 1-8 Golden Week break; Stoxx 600 636 (-0.3%) at midday, ASML flat at EUR 1,603. Brent rebounded 2.6% to about $98.7 (December contract; expiring November near $103) and WTI +2.1% to $91.3 after three vessels were hit by projectiles in Hormuz; Iran is reviewing a US counter-proposal to its seven-day plan with the gap now on sequencing, the DOE is releasing a final 40 mb SPR tranche (bids due Oct 6) and Trump is weighing a diesel export curb with US diesel at $6.53/gal. Next 48h (AEST): Micron FQ4 results after the US close, call Thu 06:30, consensus revenue $51.5b and EPS $31.83; BoJ Tankan Thu 09:50; RBA Financial Stability Review Thu 11:30; BYD September sales Thu; Trump's $54b Korea Alaska LNG announcement Thu 05:30; ISM manufacturing (prior 54.6) and Waller Fri 00:00, Jefferson Fri 03:30, Bowman Fri 05:00, Cook Fri 05:30; US September payrolls Fri 22:30 (prior +162k, unemployment 4.1%); Tesla Q3 deliveries Fri.

AMZN.reason: Up 1.6% in the first hour Wednesday after Rosenblatt raised its target to $360 and Synopsys signed a multi-year IP deal covering Trainium, Graviton and Nitro. Both back the custom-silicon and ads-resilience thesis; nothing to change.

AXOS.reason: Flat (+0.05%) early Wednesday with no company news since the Oct 29 results date. Cooler core PCE roughly halved October hike odds, which eases the funding-cost worry a touch; hold into the print.

BABA.reason: Up 0.6% Wednesday morning and still down about 27% in 2026 after missing adjusted EPS in each of the last five reports. Nearing Beijing approval to buy Nvidia RTX PRO 5500 chips is a small plus, but the November 25 print needs to end the miss streak before this moves off watch.

ENPH.reason: Up 5.5% in the first hour with no company news; reads as rate-relief buying after core PCE undershot. Citi trimmed its target to $37 on Tuesday and a StockStory screen flagged two years of falling unit volumes. A bounce, not a thesis change.

FIGR.reason: Down 0.7% early Wednesday. Aletheia started coverage at Buy on Tuesday with a target of $49, calling the on-chain lending model highly profitable and unlevered. One more supportive voice; no change.

GOOGL.reason: Up 2.5% Wednesday morning, the strongest of the group, after Google started paying about 100 publishers for content that feeds AI Overviews, Gemini and AI Mode. That trims the publisher-litigation overhang around AI search; keep adding.

LDI.reason: Up 1.0% intraday but the 30-year fixed sits at 7.58%, the highest since November 2023, and the cooler PCE print barely moved mortgage bonds (10-year 5.245%, flat). Origination volume stays pinned; keep trimming.

META.reason: Down 1.7% Wednesday morning after the NYT reported Meta labels its AI data centers experimental to claim research tax credits while pitching them to investors as proven. Headline risk, not a thesis change; hold.

MRVL.reason: Down 1.9% Wednesday morning with no company news, giving back part of Tuesday's gain ahead of the October 6 analyst day. Seaport started coverage at Buy with a target of $270, but the stock is up roughly 210% this year so we hold rather than add.

MU.reason: Up 0.9% Wednesday morning into the fiscal Q4 print tonight; options price a 7.9% move either way against an 8.1% average over the last four reports. Consensus is about $51.5 billion revenue, and the Netlist ITC filing has drawn no Micron response yet; hold through the print.

NFLX.reason: Down 0.4% early Wednesday, giving back a slice of Tuesday's upgrade bounce. No new company news; Q3 results are the next real test. Hold.

NVDA.reason: Up 1.7% Wednesday morning on the soft PCE print and CoreWeave putting Vera Rubin NVL72 into production. DeepSeek and Huawei open-sourcing a CUDA alternative for Ascend is a long-run risk, but China is already near zero share for Nvidia, so nothing here changes the hold.

RKT.reason: Down 0.8% early Wednesday. Adopting VantageScore 4.0 from Q4 widens the borrower pool at the margin, but with the 30-year at 7.58% volume is the problem, not scoring. Stay on watch.

TSM.reason: Up 0.3% Wednesday morning as Reuters sources say TSMC is evaluating a Texas site on top of the $265 billion Arizona plan with four or more further fabs. More US capacity commitments keep the customer pipeline locked in; stay on add.

STRIPE.reason: Marked 10 years in Japan on Sep 30 with Managed Payments, five local QR wallets, Tap to Pay on Android and Capital (2027); 150,000 Japanese businesses on the platform. No new round or tender reported; mark unchanged.

OPENAI.reason: Regulatory heat rose overnight: an FTC probe into OpenAI and Anthropic safety practices, the LASST civil suit over the Hugging Face breach, and a NYT report that staff warnings were ignored. Altman says no IPO until safety claims hold; the reported $30B raise at $1.4T is still only in talks, so the mark stays at the last closed basis.

headlines: US core PCE cooled to 3.0% in August against 3.3% expected; October Fed hike odds fell to about 35% and Nasdaq opened higher.
Micron reports Thu 6:30am AEST: consensus $51.5B revenue, options price a 7.9% move. SK hynix, Teradyne and ASML ride on it.
FTC opened a safety probe into OpenAI and Anthropic; Altman says no IPO until models stop going rogue.
Alphabet up 2.5% after Google began paying about 100 publishers for AI search content; Meta down 1.7% on an NYT tax-credit report.
CFTC pushed CME's GPU rental futures past Oct 5, decision due Nov 9. H100 index at a new high, Blackwell premium narrowing.
Amazon up 1.6% on a Synopsys custom-silicon deal; Enphase up 5.5% on rate relief; mortgage rates still 7.58%.
